info.title: Centrify Identity Platform API
info.description:
This site provides basic reference material for the Centrify Identity Platform API. The API calls are grouped by category – click **Show/Hide** to view or hide the list of calls for each category. Click any call to expand the information for that call, **Expand Operations** to expand the information for all calls in that category, or **List Operations** to return to list view. 
 
To  try out any of the calls:

1.      Click the **Model Schema** box to transfer the data to the payload box (or enter data in the parameter boxes).

2.      In **payload**, replace the field value-type descriptions with actual values. 

3.      Click **Try it out!** to execute the call.
 
Note that you must be logged in to execute any calls. If you are not logged in, you can see all the reference material but the **Try it out!** button is not available to call the API. 
 
Click **Model** to view a description of each field in the response or payload, and click **Model Schema** to view the schema again.
 
For more information, see [developer site](http://developer.centrify.com).

info.title: Centrify Identity Platform API
info.description:
This site provides basic reference material for the Centrify Identity Platform API. The API calls are grouped by category – click **Show/Hide** to view or hide the list of calls for each category. Click any call to expand the information for that call, **Expand Operations** to expand the information for all calls in that category, or **List Operations** to return to list view. 
 
To  try out any of the calls:

1.      Click the **Model Schema** box to transfer the data to the payload box (or enter data in the parameter boxes).

2.      In **payload**, replace the field value-type descriptions with actual values. 

3.      Click **Try it out!** to execute the call.
 
Note that you must be logged in to execute any calls. If you are not logged in, you can see all the reference material but the **Try it out!** button is not available to call the API. 
 
Click **Model** to view a description of each field in the response or payload, and click **Model Schema** to view the schema again.
 
For more information, see [developer site](http://developer.centrify.com).

For more information, see [developer site](http://developer.centrify.com).

This site provides basic reference material for the Centrify Identity Platform API. The API calls are grouped by category – click **Show/Hide** to view or hide the list of calls for each category. Click any call to expand the information for that call, **Expand Operations** to expand the information for all calls in that category, or **List Operations** to return to list view. 
 
To  try out any of the calls:

1.      Click the **Model Schema** box to transfer the data to the payload box (or enter data in the parameter boxes).

2.      In **payload**, replace the field value-type descriptions with actual values. 

3.      Click **Try it out!** to execute the call.
 
Note that you must be logged in to execute any calls. If you are not logged in, you can see all the reference material but the **Try it out!** button is not available to call the API. 
 
Click **Model** to view a description of each field in the response or payload, and click **Model Schema** to view the schema again.
 
For more information, see [developer site](http://developer.centrify.com).

firstCode.description: The first of two consecutive token codes that will be used to resynchronize the token

secondCode.description: The second of two consecutive token codes that will be used to resynchronize the token

tokenId.description: The UUID of the token to be resynchronized

post.description:
Resynchronizing requires two consecutive token codes
            (which helps to ensure that the caller is in physical possesion of the token, not just of a
            single copied token code).  Assuming that the supplied token codes can be found, TOTP resync
            will compute a new interval delta value that will be stored with the token, and HOTP resync
            will find the matching counter value (always looking forward, never backward) and update
            the counter stored with the token.
            
            Caller must either own the OATH token or be an administrator

This site provides basic reference material for the Centrify Identity Platform API. The API calls are grouped by category – click **Show/Hide** to view or hide the list of calls for each category. Click any call to expand the information for that call, **Expand Operations** to expand the information for all calls in that category, or **List Operations** to return to list view. 
 
To  try out any of the calls:

1.      Click the **Model Schema** box to transfer the data to the payload box (or enter data in the parameter boxes).

2.      In **payload**, replace the field value-type descriptions with actual values. 

3.      Click **Try it out!** to execute the call.
 
Note that you must be logged in to execute any calls. If you are not logged in, you can see all the reference material but the **Try it out!** button is not available to call the API. 
 
Click **Model** to view a description of each field in the response or payload, and click **Model Schema** to view the schema again.
 
For more information, see [developer site](http://developer.centrify.com).

info.title: Centrify Identity Platform API
info.description:
This site provides basic reference material for the Centrify Identity Platform API. The API calls are grouped by category – click **Show/Hide** to view or hide the list of calls for each category. Click any call to expand the information for that call, **Expand Operations** to expand the information for all calls in that category, or **List Operations** to return to list view. 
 
To  try out any of the calls:

1.      Click the **Model Schema** box to transfer the data to the payload box (or enter data in the parameter boxes).

2.      In **payload**, replace the field value-type descriptions with actual values. 

3.      Click **Try it out!** to execute the call.
 
Note that you must be logged in to execute any calls. If you are not logged in, you can see all the reference material but the **Try it out!** button is not available to call the API. 
 
Click **Model** to view a description of each field in the response or payload, and click **Model Schema** to view the schema again.
 
For more information, see [developer site](http://developer.centrify.com).

post.description:
When things are going smoothly, you can expect to get a 'StartNextChallenge' or 'LoginSuccess' response, however the system may (at any time)
            return a new Mfa Package which may add, remove or change challenges. Failure cases typically result in an 'Undefined' error message when things are
            misconfigured and a "LoginFailure' message when incorrect answers have terminated the session (which may have been sent in previous calls to this API).

This site provides basic reference material for the Centrify Identity Platform API. The API calls are grouped by category – click **Show/Hide** to view or hide the list of calls for each category. Click any call to expand the information for that call, **Expand Operations** to expand the information for all calls in that category, or **List Operations** to return to list view. 
 
To  try out any of the calls:

1.      Click the **Model Schema** box to transfer the data to the payload box (or enter data in the parameter boxes).

2.      In **payload**, replace the field value-type descriptions with actual values. 

3.      Click **Try it out!** to execute the call.
 
Note that you must be logged in to execute any calls. If you are not logged in, you can see all the reference material but the **Try it out!** button is not available to call the API. 
 
Click **Model** to view a description of each field in the response or payload, and click **Model Schema** to view the schema again.
 
For more information, see [developer site](http://developer.centrify.com).

CommandId.description: If specified, only return privilege elevation assignments for privilege elevation command with this ID.  You cannot specify both Command and CommandId

ScopeType.description:
Specifies whether to search for privilege elevation assignments that are effective on system set or a specific system.  Specify:
                            "Collection" to search for all privilege elevation assignments that are effective for the system set specified in "Scope".
                            "System" to search for all privilege elevation assignments that are effective for the system specified in "Scope"

Scope.description:
scope of rule. Values:
                         1. If "ScopeType" is "Collection", UUID of collection should be specified.
                         2. If "ScopeType" is "System", UUID of system should be specified.

Command.description: If specified, only return privilege elevation assignment for this privilege elevation command name.  You cannot specify both Command and CommandId

post.description:
1. "Starts" and "Expires" are returned only if there is any value in the assignment.
            2. UI can call this UI to enumerate all the effective privilege elevation assignments on a system/system set.
            3. If neither "Command" or "CommandId" is specified, this function returns ALL effective privilege elevation assignments on a system/system set.
post.summary: Enumerate all privilege elevation assignments that are effective for a specific scope

ErrorID.description: Unique support identifier for this occurrence of an error

Result.description: List of privilege elevation assignments that met the search criteria

ID.description: ID of the privilege elevation assignment object

PrivilegeElevationCommand.description: Name privilege elevation command collection (if IsPrivilegeElevationCollection is true) or privilege elevation command (if IsPrivilegeElevationCollection is false)

IsPrivilegeElevationCollection.description: whether this is a privilege elevation command or a privilege elevation command collection

ScopeType.description: whether the assignment is for a system or a system set.  Must be Collection, or System

Scope.description: scope of rule. Must be specified if scope is Collection or System.

ScopeName.description: Name of system/system set or global

BypassChallenge.description: Whether user can execute the privilege elevation command without challenge

Starts.description: Start time for temporary grant specified in UTC using ISO 8601 format.  Example: 2020-10-21T15:09:10Z

Expires.description: Expiration time for temporary grant specified in UTC using ISO 8601 format. Example: 2020-10-21T15:09:10Z

System.description: name or UUID of target machine that the privilege command will run on.

TargetOS.description: OS platform for the requested system.  Only 'Windows' and 'Linux' are supported

User.description: UPN of user who requests to run the privilege command

post.description:
1. Since this is a Read/Query operation, HTTP Get method is used.
            2. In version 1, both "System" and "User" are required parameters.  This allows us to narrow the search for specify user on specify computers.  We may relax this to support "all" in "System" and "User" in future.  However, we
               need to consider the performance/scalability implications when there are thousands of computers and thousands of users.
            3. In future versions, additional information about each rule will be returned as key/value pairs in each item.  Example of such information includes umask settings, required checksum/signature of the executable etc.
            4. The caller can be a machine service account or an authenticated user.
               a. If the caller is the machine service account, the request is sent from cagent.  The request is allowed only when the caller is the machine service account for "system".  This means that the administrator of one client
                  system cannot find out what is available as privilege elevation commands on another system.

ScopeType.description: Scope of requested privilege elevation assignment.  Must be "System" or "Collection"

Scope.description: Name of the system or collection where privilege elevation command is requested.

StartGrantValue.description: number of StartTimeInterval units when assignment starts after approval. Used when "AssignmentType" is "temp"

EndTime.description: time when assignment ends.  Specifies as "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.000Z".  Used when "AssignmentType" is "window"

StartTimeInterval.description: unit for assignment starts after approval in minutes.  Specify 60 for hour, 1440 for day. Used when "AssignmentType" is "temp"

EndTimeInterval.description: unit for assignment duration in minutes. Specify 60 for hour, 1440 for day.  Used when "AssignmentType" is "temp"

StartTime.description: time when assignment starts.  Specifies as "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.000Z". Used when "AssignmentType" is "window"

EndGrantValue.description: number of EndTimeInterval units for duration.  Used when "AssignmentType" is "temp"

IsCommandCollection.description: Whether the "Command" requested is a collection.

User.description: UPN of user who requests the workflow approval request

post.description:
1. This is similar to REST API JobFlow/StartJob.  The difference is that the caller of this API must be the service account of a client, and the 
            actual user is specified in the "User" parameter in the payload.  Internally, this function validates the input parameters and then runs the 
            job script as the actual user who requests the workflow request.
            This allows the same job script to be used when we allow the user to submit the workflow request from UI portal, where JobFlow/StartJob API is
            used to start the job.
            2. CommandID is used to identify the command instead of command name.  The reason is that the command name maybe I18N already so may not be easily
            handled by Linux systems which use UTF-8 instead of simple UCS-2 as in windows...
            When we support user selection of commands to request workflow request on, the backend should send out a list of names with UUID.  The UI displays
            the name and let user to select the item.  The sudo plugin needs to return the corresponding UUID.
            3. Using collection as scope type is not supported yet in v1.

Expires.description:
If the permission to execute is temporary, specifies the expiration time in ISO 8601 format. 
                    Example: 2020-10-21T15:09:10Z.  Note that the caller has to convert the time to UTC.

Starts.description:
If the permission to execute is temporary, specifies the start time in ISO 8601 format. 
                    Example: 2020-10-21T15:09:10Z.  Note that the caller has to convert the time to UTC.

Principal.description: Name of user/group/role in assignment.  Either "PrincipalId" or "Principal" must be specified.

PrincipalId.description: UUID of user/group/role in assignment.  Either "PrincipalId" or "Principal" must be specified.

BypassChallenge.description: Whether user can execute the privilege elevation command without challenge

post.description:
1. In v1, there is only one privilege elevation command.
            2. If additional columns are added to privilegeelevationassignment table in future for whatever reasons, they need to be optional columns and will be specified as
               additional optional parameters to this API.
            3. In v2, a new API will be added to grant user/group/role permission to run commands specified in a privilege elevation command collection.
            4. When adding permanent privilege elevation assignments (i.e., "Starts" and "Expires" are not specified), the REST API checks if there is any existing permanent privilege elevation assignment for the same command to the same principal and scope already exists, and throws an exception if it finds out.
               However, no distributed lock is taken for this check due to performance reason.  So, there is still a slight chance that it may not catch this unusual case.  However, this situation is handled
               by privilege elevation.  It will calculate the effective permission based on all matching entries.
            5. Note that it is legal to have multiple temporary privilege elevation asignments for the same command to the same principal and scope.
            6. There is no support for dynamic system set.

AgentVersion.description: Version of the agent performing the enrollment

Owner.description: Name of a user or CIP role to set as the owner of the agent profile. The owner impacts what users can manage or take over the profile

FQDN.description: Either the FQDN or IP address of the machine being enrolled

Sets.description: List of system sets to add the created system to:

DeviceID.description: Device ID of the enrolling machine. Should only be provided by Mac agents

ResourceName.description: Name the PAS system corresponding to the enrolled machine should have. If the Suffix argument is supplied, the final name of the system will be in the form '[name]@[suffix]'. Otherwise, the final name will be in the form '[name]'

Overwrite.description: Whether an agent profile take over attempt is made if the enrollment would result in such a scenario

ResourceSetting.description: JSON encoded settings the corresponding system should have. At minimum, the 'ComputerClass' and 'SessionType' values should be provided

2.      In **payload**, replace the field value-type descriptions with actual values. 

3.      Click **Try it out!** to execute the call.
 
Note that you must be logged in to execute any calls. If you are not logged in, you can see all the reference material but the **Try it out!** button is not available to call the API. 
 
Click **Model** to view a description of each field in the response or payload, and click **Model Schema** to view the schema again.

This site provides basic reference material for the Centrify Identity Platform API. The API calls are grouped by category – click **Show/Hide** to view or hide the list of calls for each category. Click any call to expand the information for that call, **Expand Operations** to expand the information for all calls in that category, or **List Operations** to return to list view. 
 
To  try out any of the calls:

1.      Click the **Model Schema** box to transfer the data to the payload box (or enter data in the parameter boxes).

2.      In **payload**, replace the field value-type descriptions with actual values. 

3.      Click **Try it out!** to execute the call.
 
Note that you must be logged in to execute any calls. If you are not logged in, you can see all the reference material but the **Try it out!** button is not available to call the API. 
 
Click **Model** to view a description of each field in the response or payload, and click **Model Schema** to view the schema again.
 
For more information, see [developer site](http://developer.centrify.com).
